info.title: Attome XRM API
info.description: The Attome XRM platform's HTTP API. Entity record shapes under `/api/v1/{entity}` are resolved from each deployment's runtime metadata (D-003) and therefore cannot be enumerated statically — those operations document the generic envelope only. Fetch `GET /api/v1/schema/{logicalname}` for a live entity's fields.

get.description:
Every published agent object that declares a hand-off contract, with its role and its input and
output schemas, for trusted partners; an agent without a contract takes no outside work.

200.description: Agents that take outside work, with their contracts

post.description:
Checks the input against the agent's contract and runs one bounded turn of the agent in a session
of its own, answering with the contract's output.

404.description: No published agent with this id

422.description: The agent takes no outside work, or cannot start a session

429.description: A budget or daily limit is used up

get.summary: Lists the actions this caller may invoke.
get.description:
Filtered by license, privilege, and the kill-switch — the same conditions
the gate applies to an invocation. A tool a caller can see but not invoke
wastes a turn for a model and misleads a human, so the list and the gate
must not disagree.

post.summary: Invokes an action as the calling human.
post.description:
There is no way to invoke as anything else: `ActionContext::user` takes the
caller's own `SecurityContext` and there is no service-principal overload
(I-3). The agent path — which supplies a risk ceiling and a taint flag —
arrives with agent sessions (TODO-039) and goes through the same
`dispatch`.

404.description: Unknown, unlicensed, or disabled action

422.description: Request failed validation

x-audit-exempt.note: the mandatory Ai+Execute event `dispatch` writes is agent-attribution-gated (ctx.is_agent(), C19/D-541 rule 4) and this route always invokes as the plain calling human (ActionContext::user, see this fn's own doc comment) — never an agent session — so that write never fires here; whatever the invoked action itself mutates is audited by that action's own executor (e.g. a record write goes through entity_crud)

post.description:
Runs the published custom action `custom.{name}` as the calling person, after checking the
arguments against its input schema (every problem by field). A consequential action needs an
`Idempotency-Key` and `X-Confirm: true`. A finished action answers 200; one that waits for a
confirmation, an approval or an undo window answers 202.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The custom action's name (its id without `custom.`)

parameters.name: X-Confirm
parameters.description: `true` once the person confirmed a consequential action; without it the action answers `confirmation_required`

202.description: The action waits for a confirmation, an approval or its undo window

403.description: Caller lacks a privilege the action requires

404.description: No published custom action by that name

422.description: Arguments that do not fit the schema, or a missing Idempotency-Key

x-audit-exempt.note: as /api/v1/actions/{id}/invoke: the route invokes as the calling human, never an agent session, so dispatch's agent-gated Ai+Execute event never fires here; what the custom action's flow changes is audited by the flow's own steps

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: One-based: page 1 is the first page.

get.summary:
`GET /api/v1/ai/conversations/{id}/stream` — the conversation's semantic
events as Server-Sent Events: every stored event after the cursor, in
ordinal order, then new ones as they commit (C10-A, I-14, row A-12).
get.description:
**Authorized before the first frame (I-20).** The conversation is resolved
for the caller before the response starts: an unknown conversation, or
someone else's, is an ordinary `404` with no stream.

**A projection of the log.** Every frame with an `id` is a committed event.
Replay and live-follow are one loop over `ordinal > cursor`, and a
conversation's events commit in ordinal order, so the handoff from replay
to live neither skips nor repeats one.

**Token deltas (C11 B3).** While following live, the stream also relays
`message.delta` frames — `{turn_id, text}`, **with no `id`**, so a delta
never moves the client's `Last-Event-ID` and a reconnect replays durable
events only (I-14, A-78). A delta for a turn whose `message.completed`
this stream has already sent is dropped: the answer supersedes it (A-79).
When Redis is unavailable there are no deltas and nothing else changes.

**Drain (AB7-T5).** When this node starts draining, the stream sends one
`reconnect` frame — `{retry_ms}`, 500 to 3000 ms, with no `id` — and
closes, so a restart is never held open by a chat. The client waits that
long and reopens from its last durable ordinal (`Last-Event-ID` or
`after`), landing on a node that is not draining.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Replay events with an ordinal greater than this (exclusive). Absent:
the `Last-Event-ID` header, else `0` — the whole log.

200.description: Server-Sent Events: each frame's `id` is the event ordinal, its `event` the event type, its `data` a StreamEventView

The gate requires a human to confirm this specific invocation before it

proposal.description:
M35 v1 C3 — present only for an action that declares one
([`Action::confirmation_proposal`]): the normalized proposal, for
display only. Model-authored, so render it as untrusted plain
text. It carries no id, token or handle and authorizes nothing:
confirming means the human invoking the action themselves.

oneOf.description:
The gate requires four-eyes approval (D-195). Nothing has executed;
`dispatch` has already raised the `attome_approval` request itself (the
gate decision's own doc comment always said this — closing the gap
where nothing actually did it). `approval_id` is the handle a caller
polls or an approver UI lists.

AH8: held for its undo window. Nothing has executed yet; it runs at
`run_at` unless cancelled (`POST /api/v1/ai/deferred-actions/{id}/cancel`)
and is re-checked first.

V2-D702: staged for the person's review with the session's other
staged actions. Nothing has executed, and nothing will until they
apply it (`POST /api/v1/ai/deferred-actions/apply`).

input_schema.description:
M101 slice 3 — the action's argument contract as a JSON Schema
document, parsed rather than passed through as a string so a consumer
reads structured JSON instead of re-parsing an escaped blob.

Published, not enforced: validation lives in each executor (see
`ActionDescriptor::input_schema`). This is what a tool-listing consumer
— a model picking a tool, an agent-builder UI, an external tool
protocol — needs in order to call an action correctly on the first try.

`value_type = Object` is required, not cosmetic: `serde_json::Value` is
a recursive enum, and letting utoipa derive an inline schema for it
here overflowed even `main.rs`'s 64 MB schema-generation stack
(`server --print-openapi` aborted with 0xC00000FD). Declaring it as a
free-form object stops the recursion and is also the truthful
description — a JSON Schema document is an arbitrary object.

to choose from, deliberately: everything else in a provider's listing
(pricing, ownership, capability flags) varies per protocol and is authored

The transport half — the request, the capped body read, the parsing and the
masking — lives in `attome_inference::list_models` (BIN-D3), because a
provider record and `config.inference.generation` describe the same kind of
destination and must not disagree about how it is reached. This type stays
here because it is the API's wire shape (`ToSchema`), which the transport
crate has no business knowing about.

holds, and what the D-491 approval gate matches on.

Effect.description:

[`RiskTier`] because they answer different questions: `Effect` decides
whether an air-gapped deployment can run it at all (I-7), `RiskTier`
decides who has to approve it.

ErrorDetails.description:
`ErrorResponse.details`: its shape depends on the `error` code —
a list of [`FieldError`] on `validation_error`, [`RuleViolationDetails`] on
`rule_violation`, [`FieldLockedDetails`] on `field_locked` and
`field_locked_required` (D-789).

ErrorResponse.description: Standard error envelope. `error` is a stable machine-readable code; `message` is human-readable and never contains internal detail.

current_state.description:
Present on a version conflict: the server's current row for the
fields the caller touched, as a JSON object. The owning engine filters
sensitive columns out before building it (BTY-16c's precondition), so
this is a deliberate filtered projection — never a raw row dump.

current_version.description:
Present on a version conflict: the `row_version` the server currently
holds, so a caller can re-read and retry instead of guessing what the
winner wrote. Omitted when the conflict is not version-based.

oneOf.description:
Structured detail, shaped by `error` (see [`ErrorDetails`]): every
field-level failure on a `validation_error` response when the raiser
has a field list, so a form can render them all at once; every firing
rule on a `rule_violation` response from a business rule; every
refused field on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`. Omitted
otherwise.

error.description:
Stable machine-readable code — `not_found`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`,
`attribute_not_writable`, `limit_exceeded`,
`conflict`, `version_conflict`, `duplicate_detected`, `idempotency_conflict`,
`validation_error`, `customer_tests_failed`, `feature_unavailable`, `feature_hidden`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, `overloaded`, `capability_unavailable`,
`metadata_authoring_locked`, `transition_not_allowed`,
`rule_violation`, `field_locked`, `field_locked_required`,
`reauth_required`, `server_timeout`, `query_timeout`, `read_only`, `payload_too_large`,
`request_rejected`, `invalid_cursor`, `resync_needed`, `cascade_restricted`,
`idempotency_outcome_unknown`, `idempotency_replay_unavailable`,
`method_not_allowed`, or
`internal_error` — one per `AppError` variant (`FieldLocked` answers
two: plain and required) (`attome-types/src/error.rs`); M01 Core C-23
found this list four codes short of the taxonomy it documents.

errors.description:
Every field-level failure on a `validation_error`, as
`{attribute, rule, message, fix}`.

field.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the first
refused field (every one is in `details.fields`); on
`attribute_not_writable` (Q15-T4): the attribute the caller may not
write.

hidden.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected`: how many more matches the caller may
not read.

instance.description: The request path the problem happened at.

matches.description:
Present on `duplicate_detected` (A15-T4): the existing records the
save matches that the caller may read (record, rule, score).

request_id.description:
Present on responses that passed through the request-id middleware
(D-043); absent on the few pre-middleware rejection paths.

retry_after_sec.description:
Present on a `rate_limit_exceeded` response when the limiter knows its
window: seconds to wait before retrying, equal by construction to the
`Retry-After` header on the same response (BTY-11a). Omitted when the
limit that was hit has no known window.

retryable.description:
Whether the same request may succeed later (the error catalogue's
verdict for `code`).

rule_id.description:
Present on a `rule_violation` response (D-472): the id of the
`xrm_core_rule` whose failing expression produced this 422, so a
client can highlight or re-check the exact rule without parsing
`message`. Omitted on every other code, and on any response that
does not name a rule.
Also present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` (D-789): the
business rule that locks `field`.

rule_name.description:
Present on `field_locked` / `field_locked_required`: the display name
of the rule that locks `field`.

title.description:
A short title for `code` in the request's language (Z14-T3), e.g.
`The resource was not found.`

type.description: Z14-T1 (RFC 9457): `about:blank`; the problem is named by `code`.

FeedbackStats.description: Votes on turn answers written in the window.

answers.description: Rateable messages: an assistant message with a terminal state.

rated_answers.description: Answers with at least one vote.

FeedbackView.description: The caller's current vote on one answer.

api_protocol.description:
The protocol the listing was performed under, echoed so a UI can label

FieldError.description:
One field-level failure inside `ErrorResponse.details` (BTY-16b): the
field the caller sent, a stable machine-readable `code` the client maps
to localized text (e.g. `required`, `too_long`, `invalid_format`,
`not_allowed`), and the English server-side `message`.

A list, not a single error, so one 422 can answer with every bad field at
once (BTY-F11) instead of making a form discover them one round-trip at a
time.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable failure code for this field, independent of
the message text.

field.description:
The offending field, as the caller addressed it (e.g. `email` or
`amount`).

message.description: Human-readable, English, server-side detail for this field.

FieldLockedDetails.description:
`details` of a `field_locked` / `field_locked_required` response: every
refused field, the first being the one the top-level `field` names.

GovernanceView.description:

state.description:
`"live"` | `"paused"` | `"ended"` — ended covers revoked, ended and

args.description:
The action's own arguments. Shape is per-action and validated by the
executor, not here — a handler that understood every action's argument

AH8: hold the action this many seconds (30 to 86400) before it runs,

id.description: Absent for a notification, which takes no response.

One field a business rule locks for the writer (D-789 §3.5): `effect` is

agent_retrieval_mode.description:
The mode the session's agent definition is configured with **now**, for
comparison only: it reaches the next session started from that
definition, never this one. `unrecognised` when the definition holds a
value a new session would refuse to start with; `None` when the session
has no definition or the definition row no longer exists.

allowed_action_ids.description:
The session's effective allow-list, exactly as snapshotted at start.
`None` means "whatever the ceiling permits"; `[]` means nothing — a
supervisor reading the dashboard must see the difference.

capability_pack_refs.description:

versions) produced the grants above. Never consulted for
authorization; shown so an operator can say where a grant came from.

retrieval_mode.description:
D-561 §5: the knowledge retrieval mode this session **uses** —
`tool_invoked` | `pre_retrieved`, resolved from its agent definition
when it started and stored on the row. Nothing changes it afterwards.

PendingView.description: Why a turn stopped for a human.

messages.description: The messages in order, as sent: `role` and `content`.

suggestion_id.description:
The row in `ai_suggestion_outcome` this suggestion was logged as.
The caller reports the human's decision against it.

RebuildRange.description: The rebuild job's payload: the UTC days to recount, both included.

RecordContext.description:
The record the user is looking at, sent by the panel as a navigation hint
(I-19). Never authorization: see the module doc.

RecordRun.description: One record's outcomes, step by step.

error.description: Why the record stopped early, when it did.

ReviewDecision.description:
Which staged actions a review decision covers: one agent session's, or
chosen ones (at most [`MAX_REVIEW_IDS`]).

undo_window_seconds.description:
Apply only: hold the applied actions this many seconds (30 to 86400)
before they run, cancellable; omit to run them now.

RiskTier.description:
How much damage an action can do, which decides what has to happen before
it runs. This is the single most important field on a descriptor.

The tiers are ordered, and the ordering is load-bearing: an agent session
carries a ceiling and the gate compares against it. Adding a tier means
deciding where it sits relative to `Consequential`, which is a decision
somebody has to make deliberately.

RollbackPreview.description: AH2-T4: what rolling an agent back would do.

session_ids.description: The agent's sessions since the time.

RollbackSince.description: AH2-T4: when to roll an agent back from.

since.description: Undo what the agent did at or after this time (UTC, ISO-8601).

RuleFailure.description:
One business-rule `error` policy that fired (D-789 §3.3), inside a
`rule_violation` body's `details.rules`. Carries names and the rule's own
message, never a record value.

field.description: The field the policy is attached to, when it names one.

rule_name.description: The rule's display name (its name when it has none).

RuleViolationDetails.description:
`details` of a `rule_violation` response (D-789): the field of the first
failing policy, when it names one, and every blocking `error` policy that
fired, the first (by rule display order) being the one `rule_id` names.

RunStarted.description: What a started run returns at once (N7-T1).

status.description:
`running`: follow `GET /api/v1/ai/conversations/{id}/stream` for its
steps and its end state.

RunToolCall.description: One tool call inside a turn of a run (N29-T1).

invocation_outcome.description: The invocation ledger's outcome for it, when it reached the ledger.

RunTree.description: A session's whole run as one tree (N29-T1).

oneOf.description:
Optional: the record the user is looking at — a navigation hint,
**never authorization** (I-19, row A-66). Shape-checked only, never
looked up, and stored as one fixed line in the user's message.

money_cap_minor.description:
Minor units of `currency`; requires the action to declare a money
argument, or every invocation asks first.

row_version.description:
The row's current `row_version` when replacing a row; a stale one is
refused with 409.

time_zone.description: IANA zone for the hours, such as `Asia/Riyadh`; UTC when unset.

undo_seconds.description: Seconds an `act_with_undo` action waits before it runs (30 to 86400).

api_key.description:
The provider's API key. Write-only: no route ever returns it, and the
response carries only its last four characters.

is_set.description:
Q18-T6: a key is stored. The key itself, or any part of it, is never
returned.

updated_at.description: When the stored key was set.

reason.description: Why — shown beside the switch and recorded in the audit event.

SpendLine.description: One money window's month so far.

cap.description: The cap, in the price unit.

forecast.description: Where the window's spend is heading over a whole month.

key.description: The feature id or agent id; empty for the deployment.

percent.description: `spent` as a percentage of `cap` (100 or more: refusing).

spent.description: Spent inside the window, in the price unit.

degrade_at_percent.description: Percent of a cap at which generations are shortened.

model.description: The generation model the prices apply to.

priced.description: Whether that model has a price; without one nothing is counted.

allowed_action_ids.description: Optional. Omitted or `null`: whatever the ceiling permits. `[]`: nothing.

mode.description:
Optional (N1-T1): `"develop"` builds — the metadata tools and reads,
so every change is a draft and no record is written; `"run"` acts —
everything but the metadata edit tools. Omitted: no narrowing. It only
narrows `allowed_action_ids`, never widens it.

risk_ceiling.description:
**Required.** `"read"` | `"reversible"` | `"consequential"` — the same
explicit ceiling `POST /agents/{id}/sessions` takes. The agent policy
still bounds it; it never grants anything the caller does not hold.

allowed_action_ids.description: Optional; narrows the agent's own tools further.

max_steps.description:
The most tool steps the run may take (capped by the platform's own
bound); omitted: the platform's bound.

task.description: What the agent is to do.

agent.description:
Optional (V2-D487): a published `agent` metadata object whose tools
become one more allow-list. It only narrows: with
`allowed_action_ids` too, the session gets the actions in both.

allowed_action_ids.description:
Optional. Omitted or `null` means "whatever the ceiling permits"; `[]`
means the session may invoke nothing.

risk_ceiling.description:
**Required.** `"read"` | `"reversible"` | `"consequential"`. There is no
default: the person starting the session states its ceiling. It never
grants anything the caller's own privileges do not already allow.

risk.description: `Read`, `Reversible` or `Consequential`; absent for an unknown action.

StreamEventView.description:
One frame's `data`: a stored event, as the stream sends it. The frame's SSE
`id` is `ordinal` and its `event` is `type`.

content.description:
`message.completed` only: the message text, read from the message
ledger when the frame is sent — the event row stores no copy.

ordinal.description: The stream cursor: gapless per conversation.

payload.description: The event's stored payload (references and labels, never content).

type.description: One of the nine semantic event types.

edit_distance.description:
Required when `outcome = "edited"`, rejected otherwise — migration
`0118`'s CHECK ties the two together in both directions.

outcome.description:
`accepted` | `edited` | `rejected`. There is deliberately no `pending`:
a decision cannot move a row back to undecided, which is what keeps an
abandoned suggestion distinguishable from a rejected one.

recorded.description:
`false` when this decision was not the first one recorded. A
double-submit from the UI must not overwrite an accept with a reject,
so the first decision wins and the caller is told which theirs was.

SurfaceSwitchView.description: One surface as the admin screen shows it.

configured.description:
What the deployment's configuration allows. Changing it takes a
restart; this route never does.

effective.description: `configured AND runtime_enabled`, as the gate applies it.

runtime_enabled.description:
The runtime switch: `false` only when an administrator turned it off.
`null` when the switch state could not be read — which every AI
surface treats as off.

ToolCallCounts.description: One action's tool-call events in the window.

by_action.description: One row per action id, sorted by it.

agreement.description: same / (same + different); `null` before anything was compared.

different_sample.description: The latest decisions a person did differently (at most 50).

reason.description: The departure, e.g. `automatic: volume: observed 200, expected 5`.

TurnCount.description: How many turns ended one way in the last day.

citations.description: The turn's executed knowledge actions' citations (row A-56).

model_id.description: The model that wrote `text`, when one did.

terminal_state.description: One of the twelve terminal states (D-565).

awaiting.description:
Ended with `awaiting_confirmation` or `awaiting_approval`: stopped for
a human, neither a success nor a failure.

cancelled.description:
Ended with `cancelled`: the user pressed Stop (C11 B4). Neither a
success nor a failure, so counted on its own.

ended.description: `turn.completed` events in the window. Each turn ends exactly once.

failed.description: Ended with any of the other nine states.

UndoRunView.description: An undo run and a page of its items.

summary.description: Item counts by outcome, once finished.

Vote.description: Up or down, and nothing else.

Warning.description:
Something the server did that the caller should know about though the
request succeeded (a value truncated, a default applied, a page clamped):
a stable `code` and English `message`. Sent only when there is one.

portal_session.name: __Secure-wp_{portal}_session
portal_session.description: A web portal user's session cookie, issued by the portal's sign-in; `{portal}` is the portal's keyword (`wp_{portal}_session` on plain-http local dev). Valid only on that portal's own routes.

s2s_hmac.name: x-s2s-signature
s2s_hmac.description: A system-to-system call, signed. Send `x-s2s-client-id`, `x-s2s-key-id`, `x-s2s-timestamp` (Unix milliseconds, within 300 seconds of the server's clock), `x-s2s-nonce` (single use: a repeat is refused) and `x-s2s-signature`: the hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed by the hex-decoded client secret, of `METHOD`, `PATH_AND_QUERY`, the hex SHA-256 of the body, `TIMESTAMP` and `NONCE`, joined by newlines in that order.

session_cookie.name: __Host-session_token
session_cookie.description: Browser session cookie issued by POST /api/v1/auth/login. Mutating requests additionally require the CSRF conditions enforced by `middleware::csrf`.
